# `particle_voice/nn/kernels/KernelRegistry.js`

> **Source:** `agi/particle_voice/nn/kernels/KernelRegistry.js`

KernelRegistry.js — Phase 1 ParticleNN kernel infrastructure. Maps kernel name -> `shader(params)` generator, mirroring `agi/llm/kernels/KernelRegistry.js`'s design (reference only, not imported — same LLM-runtime-decoupling rule as `PipelineUtils.js`). Each generator here also declares `inputCount` (how many read-only storage bindings it expects before the single read_write output binding) so `createShaderModule`'s caller can build the matching explicit bind-group layout required for `useShaderF16` kernels (see `DeviceContract-v0.md` §8 / `KernelValidation.js`'s `createExplicitLayoutPipeline`) without re-deriving each kernel's binding count by hand.

## Classes

### `class KernelRegistry`

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `constructor()` |  |
| `list` | `list()` |  |
| `get` | `get(name)` |  |
| `generate` | `generate(name, params = {})` | Generate WGSL source for `name`, forwarding `params` (e.g. `{ useShaderF16 }`) to its generator. |
| `bindGroupLayoutEntriesFor` | `bindGroupLayoutEntriesFor(name)` | The `GPUBindGroupLayoutEntry[]` a kernel needs: uniform@0 (unless the kernel declared `hasUniform: false`, e.g. `fft1024_f32`/`ifft1024_f32`, which need no per-dispatch scalar data), then `inputCount` read-only storage bindings, then one read_write storage output binding last — matches every Phase 1/2 kernel's binding convention exactly (verified by construction in `tests/particle-voice/phase1-core.html`). |
| `createShaderModule` | `createShaderModule(device, name, params = {})` |  |

## Notes & Examples

### Where this fits in the training loop

AGI runs an **observation → brain → action → reward** loop each tick: observations are gathered from the world, a brain maps them to actions, the rig applies motion, and rewards shape the next update.

**Example: Minimal training loop**
```js
import { Agent } from 'agi/core/Agent.js';
import { World } from 'agi/env/World.js';

const world = new World();
const agent = new Agent({
  brain: 'ppo',
  observationSpace: world.observationSpace,
  actionSpace: world.actionSpace
});

for (let step = 0; step < 10000; step++) {
  const obs = world.getObservation();      // Gather observations
  const action = agent.act(obs);            // Brain decides action
  const { reward, done } = world.step(action); // Apply action, get reward
  agent.learn(obs, action, reward);         // Update from experience
  
  if (done) world.reset();
}
```

**See also:** [AGI Training Guide](/agi/training-guide.md) · [AGI Architecture](/agi/architecture.md)
